article.headline: Dell Falls 2.2% After Hours After Worst Day In Over A Year
article.deck: Dell dropped 11.3% on downgrades tied to AI-spending worries and closed below its 50-day line; still 8.2% past its 469.57 buy point, it is out of the buy range and not buyable here.
body: Dell Technologies slipped to 497.00 after hours as of 6:40 p.m. ET, down 2.2%, after a regular-session drop of 64.54, or 11.3%, to 507.93. Volume ran 1.51 times the 50-day average. Headlines called it the stock's worst day in more than a year, and Investopedia reported that Dell, HPE and NetApp slumped after downgrades on worries about AI spending. A CNN headline said AI stocks dropped after a hot inflation report bolstered bets for Fed rate hikes.

Dell sells the hardware companies use to run their computing: servers, including AI-optimized machines, along with storage and networking gear through its Infrastructure Solutions Group, and PCs and related products through its Client Solutions Group. Dell is one of the leaders the desk lists for its AI chips group, alongside Sandisk, Micron and HPE.

The quarters show why. In the July quarter, EPS rose 272.9% to 6.34 a share, and revenue jumped 57.7% to 46.97 billion. EPS rose in each of the four quarters given: 2.28, 3.37, 5.24 and then 6.34. Revenue climbed from 27.01 billion to 33.38 billion to 43.84 billion to 46.97 billion over the same stretch. The next report is due Nov. 27.

The market values Dell at 322.9 billion. The stock trades at 29.5 times trailing earnings and 17.0 times forward earnings. Even after Wednesday, shares are up 303.5% this year and 231.1% over 12 months, and Dell still ranks 99 of 99 on the desk's list.

The chart has turned. Dell broke out Aug. 12 from a 10-week cup that was 23.9% deep, with a 469.57 buy point, on volume just 0.78 times average. It ran to a 52-week high of 595.51 and now sits 14.7% below it. The close is 8.2% past the buy point, above the buy range that ended at 493.05, so the original entry is long gone. Wednesday's drop took the stock 0.9% below its 50-day line at 512.76 and well under the 21-day at 550.49. The RS line is 14.6% off its high.

Forty-four sessions after the breakout, the stock has closed below its 50-day line on heavy volume. The 200-day line is far below at 310.65. A new entry would need either a fresh base or a recovery of the 50-day line.
article.watch: Whether Dell can retake its 50-day line at 512.76 or keeps sliding toward the 493.05 top of the old buy range.

article.headline: Micron Slides 2.3% After Hours Following 4.1% Drop In Chip Sell-Off
article.deck: Micron's September breakout has failed: the stock closed 11.8% below its 1,036.23 buy point and broke its 50-day line, so there is no entry.
body: Micron fell to 893.07 after hours as of 6:40 p.m. ET, down 2.3%, extending a regular-session loss of 39.06, or 4.1%, to 914.13. Volume during the session matched the 50-day average at 1.0 times. The stock broke out Sept. 21 from a five-week flat base with a 1,036.23 buy point, on volume just 0.82 times average. Seventeen sessions later it closes 11.8% below that buy point, a failed breakout. The base's low is 887.61, set Aug. 24; the after-hours price sits just above it.

That flat base formed inside a bigger correction, and Micron remains well below its 1,255.00 peak from June 25. The 52-week high is 27.2% above Wednesday's close. The stock closed 7.0% below its 50-day line at 982.41 and under the 21-day at 1,015.86. Micron still ranks 98 of 99 on the desk's list, but the RS line has fallen 28.2% from its high.

The fundamentals have not cracked. In the May quarter, EPS rose 1,368.5% to 24.67 a share, and revenue jumped 345.7% to 41.46 billion. EPS climbed through the four quarters given, from 2.83 to 4.60 to 12.07 to 24.67. The stock trades at 4.4 times forward earnings, with a market cap of 1.03 trillion. The next report is due Dec. 23.

Wednesday's headlines put the drop in a broad chip sell-off: one said Nvidia sank as the sell-off deepened on hot inflation data, another that CoreWeave, Intel and Micron were plummeting. A separate headline quoted a description of China's competitive threat to Micron as a paper tiger.
A break of the 887.61 base low would leave the stock with no structure until a new base forms.
article.watch: Whether Micron holds the 887.61 base low or slices through it.

The stock closed 1.1% below its 52-week high of 61.66. It trades 8.0% above its 50-day line at 56.47, with the 21-day line at 58.59. The RS line hit a new high Wednesday, the only one among today's stories to do so, and Exelixis ranks 84 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 39.2% this year and 58.7% over 12 months.

In the June quarter, EPS rose 26.2% to 0.82 a share, and revenue grew 10.6% to 628.7 million. The three prior quarters earned 0.79, 0.88 and 0.69 a share. The stock trades at 14.3 times forward earnings, with a market cap of 15.1 billion. The next report is due Oct. 27.
A recent headline asked whether Exelixis is fully valued as its cabozantinib patent window comes into focus.
A close back below 59.82 would put the breakout in stalled territory.
